item: TArray<GFxValue> is wrong
evidence: GFxValue has a destructor that releases a managed value and UE3's TArray::Add hands back raw uninitialised memory, so the first ChangeType would release garbage. DisFMInvokeStep uses a fixed GFxValue Args[4]. SetStringW stores the pointer rather than a copy, so the parsed argument strings have to outlive the Invoke; they do, in the same scope. Neither fails at compile time
